### 3410111 Dilemma {#episode-3410111}

> Subtitle: He has lain down with dogs, hoping to rise without fleas.


In the dim cell, low chants rise and fall over and over until it almost feels like a natural phenomenon, like the howling of the wind.

**Constable I**: Chief, all the Yao we've arrested are here.

> 【Title card】Jail, Ancient Zhu County

A cell door creaks open slowly. The other Yao stop and look out from their cells at the three who enter.

**Cheng Heguang**: ...

**Cheng Heguang**: Hmph. This must be the true meaning of being "watched like a hawk."

**Cheng Heguang**: You may leave. I will have the victim identify the culprit.

**Constable I**: Understood.

The cell is packed with Yao. Afraid, a man presses himself fearfully against Chéng Héguāng.

Chéng grips his blade and tells the man not to be afraid, as he takes the first bold step toward them.

**Cheng Heguang**: I trust there's no need to introduce myself.

**Bird**: Of course, Chief Chéng. After all, it took us all quite some effort to sneak past you, hahahahaha.

**Bird**: Let no one say that you neglected your duties. In fact, you did such a sterling job that not even a fly could buzz through that gate.

**Bird**: A pity for you that I soar much higher than a fly! Ahahahahahaha!

The Yao all laugh, leading Chéng Héguāng to raise his blade and strike it against the cell door.

**Cheng Heguang**: Quiet!

**Cheng Heguang**: Look over them. See if you can identify the one that abducted your family.

Even with the cell door between them, the man feels surrounded by Yao; he dodges fruitlessly left then right as if to avoid their gaze.

He peeks at the jailed Yao from the corner of his eye. But each glance makes him all the more concerned.

**County Resident I**: I-I don't see them.

**Bird**: My, my, should I call you County Magistrate Chéng now? If I recall correctly, it falls outside of the duties of mere constables to interrogate suspects.

Through the bars, a bird-like Yao leans toward Chéng Héguāng.

**Bird**: Could it be that you are using this opportunity to learn the Method of Longevity for yourself? Haha!

**Cheng Heguang**: Enough of your twittering, bird. I am investigating this rumor on behalf of the people, not for myself.

**Cheng Heguang**: Nor is this a formal interrogation. I am within my rights to question any one of you.

**Bird**: Heh heh. And if I don't tell you a thing, what then, Chief Chéng?

**Bird**: Must you really be so harsh on us? Every Yao in Zhu County is scared to death of you.

**Bird**: But I know that you're not all that cruel-hearted. Could you be persuaded to let us go?

As she speaks, she puts both hands through the bars. One holds a gold bar, the other a charm. She waves them before Chéng Héguāng.

**Bird**: I can offer you both wealth and health.

**Cheng Heguang**: Fiend! I will not allow you to deceive me.

Chéng Héguāng pushes her hands aside with the back of his blade. She jumps back, staring at him tensely, then approaches once more.

**Bird**: You think it deception merely because you believe the Method of Longevity to be a false rumor.

**Bird**: But what if I tell you, it's true, hm? Take a guess at how old I am.

**Cheng Heguang**: There's no need to guess. It is said that Yao can live over a thousand years.

**Bird**: Whoever told you that knew nothing. Our lives are scarcely longer than our true forms. My own kind live and die within the age of a sparrow. Nothing more.

Surprise flashes in Chéng Héguāng's eyes. He motions for her to continue.

**Bird**: We only want a little more time in this world, Chief Chéng. Why must you stand in our way?

**Cheng Heguang**: Then should I simply allow you and your people to kill, steal, and bring chaos?

**Bird**: Me and my people?

She is stunned for a moment, then responds with a burst of laughter.

**Bird**: Hahahaha ... I see.

**Bird**: You believe the Yao to be evil.

**Cheng Heguang**: No, not universally. Yet it is Yao like you who spread these dangerous rumors in the county.

The Yao stops laughing, her neck jerking in as her feathers rise and puff out.

Filled with rage, she storms toward Chéng Héguāng, ignoring the bars.

**Bird**: It is no rumor, fool! Even if it were, what harm have we ever brought for speaking it alone? All our kind desire is to live!

**Bird**: I've done nothing wrong! Release me! Every moment is precious!

**Cheng Heguang**: You may not have taken part in these abductions, but the rumors you spread surely enticed the ones that did. I will not release you.

**Bird**: Fine, continue in your blindness, but the School of Mei will bring justice to us all.

The Yao turns fierce, beating her wings in the cell. Claw marks cover the walls.

**Cheng Heguang**: The School of Mei. That's the name of your sect, is it?

Her anger has become an incomprehensible mash of threats and insults. Chéng Héguāng stands between her and the scared man, leading him away.

> 【Title card】Study, Yamen

In the Yamen's study, the man sits shaking on a wooden chair.

**Cheng Heguang**: Calm down. Have some tea.

**County Resident I**: Th-Thank you.

He takes the tea, sips a few times, then sets it down.

**Cheng Heguang**: No need to worry; our cells are quite unbreakable.

**Cheng Heguang**: So, what more do you know of the Yao that abducted your family?

**County Resident I**: It was jabbering on about "longevity." That's all I know.

**Cheng Heguang**: This rumor is a true menace to society.

**County Resident I**: Please, Chief Chéng, please find my father. You're my only hope.

He grabs the front of Chéng Héguāng's clothes as if to kneel. But the chief constable catches him by the arms and lifts him to his feet.

**Cheng Heguang**: Please, sir. I am merely fulfilling my duty.

**Cheng Heguang**: I will find the truth. This I swear.

**County Resident I**: Thank you.

**Cheng Heguang**: Rest a while. Best not to overwork yourself.

**Cheng Heguang**: Guard!

**Constable I**: Chief.

**Cheng Heguang**: Take care of the good man. I must deliver my report on the events at the opera.

**Constable I**: Understood.

Chéng Héguāng pats the poor man's shoulder as they walk out.

A breeze follows him past the door and scatters far away.

> 【Title card】Hall, Yamen

In the great hall, a report on the case is being given to the gathered court.

**Registrar**: The female Daoist raised her sword above a woman's head, revealing the latter's true form to be that of a herbaceous entity and shifting her withered leaves into a verdant green.

**Registrar**: The Daoist then proclaimed the ability to bestow longevity upon any who joined her school. This declaration incited the crowd to a frenzy as they stampeded the stage.

**Registrar**: Later, the Daoist vanished from the scene together with the herbaceous entity. Several Yao present were detained, and the injured were escorted to the nearest clinic for treatment.

**Registrar**: In summary, the stampede has been determined to be an unforeseen incident arising from the female Daoist's use of arcane skills.

With the report concluded, the paper is folded once more and then handed over to the county magistrate.

**County Magistrate**: "Unforeseen incident"? Your lack of foresight has seen this longevity rumor spread to every corner of the county!

**County Magistrate**: Yao are flooding our lands in droves! Never in my life have I received so many reports of missing persons and acts of sedition!

**County Magistrate**: Make no mistake. This is the result of your errors!

The magistrate crumples the paper and throws it at the registrar. In response, the man bows even lower.

**County Magistrate**: *sigh* We were foolish to put our faith in you.

**County Magistrate**: Commander Lì, you are in charge of our defenses. Tell me, how should we proceed?

Lì Huìfēng had been standing nearby; he pauses, considering the details for a moment, before speaking out in a measured tone.

**Li Huifeng**: In these desperate times, I can see only one solution.

**Li Huifeng**: I would divide all constables into two shifts and have them sweep the entire county. We will locate and apprehend all Yao hiding among the populace over the next three days.

**County Magistrate**: Very good! Do you hear that? All departments will cooperate with Commander Lì! And if I hear of any misconduct, I will show no mercy!

The others hasten to agree as they bow with clasped hands.

Chéng Héguāng has been wanting to speak. Seeing his chance, he seizes it and steps forward.

**Cheng Heguang**: Honorable Magistrate, I believe we also ought to consider investigating the School of Mei.

The other clerks sneak sneering glances toward him, like a discolored bean sifted from the pile.

**County Magistrate**: And you are? Wait, I believe I recall, Chief Chéng, is it?

**County Magistrate**: And this School of Mei? A minor religious sect, yes?

**Cheng Heguang**: Yes. Please forgive me. After the report was submitted, I discovered a connection between the sect and the animal carcasses found on the streets.

**Cheng Heguang**: While in custody, a suspect admitted that the School of Mei was behind the mysterious parade connected to both the rumors and the drained carcasses.

**Cheng Heguang**: I believe this opera was another part of their scheme. If the Yao are the fruit, the School of Mei is the root.

The others look away and whisper.

**Deputy Magistrate**: And who are you to speak? Some upstart boy desperate to clear his family name?

**Registrar**: That's him alright. Just last month, he was ranting about some thief-catching scheme; the argument could be heard from the streets.

**Deputy Magistrate**: Do you remember last year? This boy nigh on knocked the doors down, insisting we include those deserters he caught in our update to the Imperial Court.

**Deputy Magistrate**: Hard to believe the magistrate allowed him to leave with his head. It seems he hasn't any sense for his position or his shame.

**Registrar**: The son of a bandit turncoat. No wonder he barks like a dog, demanding praise for his every deed.

**Registrar**: He's fooling himself if he thinks he can wash himself clean of his family's past.

Chéng Héguāng ignores their whispers and stands tall and firm as a noble pine.

**County Magistrate**: Commander Lì, thoughts on this matter?

As all else goes quiet, Lì Huìfēng clears his throat and speaks.

**Li Huifeng**: Ahem. I hold to what I've said before; the Yao pose a serious danger to the people. Our priority must be to expel them from the county.

**Li Huifeng**: What would you have us do, Your Honor?

**County Magistrate**: The matter is handed to Commander Lì. Dismissed.

**Constables**: Understood.

**Cheng Heguang**: But the School of Mei ...

The others seem prepared to leave, but Chéng Héguāng looks around anxiously, until finding the familiar shape of his commander waiting under the eaves.

**Cheng Heguang**: Commander Lì!

**Li Huifeng**: Come here, Héguāng.

Lì Huìfēng walks from the hall in long, quick strides, forcing his subordinate to hurry to keep pace.

**Li Huifeng**: Are you really so desperate for glory that you forget the chain of command?

**Li Huifeng**: How do you aim to win trust if you refuse to pay respect to your betters?

**Cheng Heguang**: I apologize, Commander.

**Cheng Heguang**: But this is a promising lead. If we don't act now, we may miss our chance.

Lì Huìfēng turns, his voice sterner than ever.

**Li Huifeng**: Do you think you're the only one with a lead on this case?

**Li Huifeng**: That no one else can do as you have done? Not even those with greater power and resources?

**Li Huifeng**: Is that why you announced your intentions for all to hear? Your heart may be pure, but others have their own designs. If your words reach the wrong ears, do you think they will sit and do nothing about it?

Chéng Héguāng's tongue twists. He had prepared for a scolding, not this.

**Cheng Heguang**: Commander, you mean ...

**Li Huifeng**: Keep digging, but do not draw any further attention.

**Li Huifeng**: That's all for today. And if your actions are brought to light, I will tell them I denied your request, understood?

**Cheng Heguang**: Yes, Commander!

He bows deeply, then straightens his posture.

**Cheng Heguang**: I will learn from your wise words.

### 3410112 Castle in the Sky {#episode-3410112}

> Subtitle: Many have heard its name, yet few know its truth.


> 【Title card】Yard, School of Mei

**Master Ren**: Come, Mayfly. You ought to familiarize yourself with our school before you begin.

**Mayfly**: Yes, Master.

Mayfly peeks out from behind the door, watching the others in the front courtyard.

**Mayfly**: It's still early in the morning, but everyone's already up and busy.

**Master Ren**: It is. Soon, you will be practicing alongside them.

The many Yao she has come to know nod to her in greeting.

**Master Ren**: The students live in the side house here, as will you. I believe you've met some of them already.

**Quick Mouse**: *squeak*

**Mayfly**: I see, ah! There's a mouse climbing up on that bamboo by the wall.

**Master Ren**: Heh. Don't be alarmed by Brother Mouse. He has taken to staying in his true form most of the day.

**Mayfly**: F-Forgive me, Brother.

**Master Ren**: I'm sure he does not mind. The School of Mei is one of the few refuges for Yao in this region. Our students are free to live in whatever form they wish. You may even choose to live as a reed, if that is what you desire.

**Mayfly**: Live in my true form. But I ...

**Master Ren**: One must learn to find fulfillment in their true nature; only then may one discern their path to the Way. It will make sense in time.

**Mayfly**: Hmm.

**Master Ren**: Come. Let us speak further in the front courtyard.

**Mayfly**: Master, where is that music coming from? I keep hearing it, but I don't see anyone playing.

**Master Ren**: You won't have need of that haste much longer, Sister Mayfly.

**Master Ren**: This is the front courtyard, where students may gather to train or rest as they like.

**Mayfly**: But no one's here.

**Master Ren**: This way.

The gardens of this land excel at artful concealment. Past the moon gate, after a few winding paths, a hidden world opens up to her.

Black eaves press down upon white rooms that enclose a square. The ground is paved with gravel, into which white marble tiles are set, forming a Bagua array.

Students in white stand atop it, playing solemn Daoist music together.

**Yam**: There she is, the new student!

**Hedgehog**: Sister Mayfly, are you feeling better?

Paper Heron waits here too. The students occasionally steal small glances at her.

She looks around, nodding to the students as she meets their eyes and greeting Mayfly in particular.

**Mayfly**: Hello, everyone, what are you all doing here?

**All Yao**: Master Rén is here too!

**All Yao**: Greetings, Master! We humbly request your guidance this day!

**Master Ren**: It's good to see you all. Please, be seated.

The crowd spreads out and sits in a ring around Master Rén. A female Yao pulls Mayfly in to sit beside her.

**Master Ren**: Revision always offers new insight. And with a new student among us today, let us begin by reviewing the stages of the Method of Longevity.

**Master Ren**: To master this art, one must attain three stages: the regulation of Qi, concentration and visualization, and the cultivation of the body.

**Master Ren**: In the first stage, we focus on the rhythm of the breath. Each of you must find the pace which best suits your constitution and nature.

**Master Ren**: Once you reach a state of meditation, we will work to concentrate the mind on an object, opening ourselves to the stimuli of the divine, as for the cultivation of the body.

Hearing this, Paper Heron interrupts Master Rén.

**Paper Heron**: That wouldn't be for the best.

**Master Ren**: Whatever do you mean, Master?

**Paper Heron**: Your students are getting ahead of themselves. Teach them the basics first, eh? A pavilion is not built from the roof down.

**Master Ren**: If I am to cover every foundational detail, I would have to start from before the White Horse School was even founded.

**Master Ren**: Unfortunately, I never walked its halls. All that I know, I learned from you. Would you do us the honor, Grandmaster?

**Master Ren**: The students would be most grateful to hear it from your lips.

Paper Heron looks around. The students wait eagerly for her words. The School of Mei seems to be thriving on the high morale of its students, and her heart is warmed by it.

**Paper Heron**: It has been quite some time since I last spoke of my old school, but I'd be happy to.

She lifts her heels and leaps gracefully into the ring before launching into her story.

**Paper Heron**: The very first attempts at achieving longevity can be traced back to ancient times, but it's enough to start with the founding of the White Horse School, eh?

**Paper Heron**: It first took shape in the late Tang Dynasty, as our founding master traveled the land collecting many rare and lost scriptures in hopes of preserving the Daoist arts for future generations.

**Paper Heron**: From those arts, he developed a method to balance Yin and Yang, and through it, discovered the secret to a long life.

**Paper Heron**: He named it The Practice of Inner Alchemy, and it later became the foundation of the White Horse School.

**Paper Heron**: Now, to perform it properly, you must work through these stages in order. Listen closely.

**Paper Heron**: The scripture says, "When one's mind is tranquil and free of distracting thoughts, all things between heaven and earth will become one with it." So, the first step is to set aside worldly concerns and seek stillness from within, for only then can one perceive the presence of the Way.

**Paper Heron**: Step two is about finding your Qi. "Life is born of the accumulation of Qi. When Qi gathers, we live; when it disperses, we perish."

**Paper Heron**: Without Qi, we can neither strengthen our bodies nor nourish our spirits, and so we cannot prolong our lives. We must spend years learning its workings, until it becomes as familiar to us as our own hands.

**Paper Heron**: The third step is to use your understanding of Qi to work its flow, guiding it until it moves in harmony with the Way.

**Paper Heron**: This step is the most crucial—when your body attunes itself to your Qi and allows you to retain it. This may take some time, but it must not be rushed.

**Paper Heron**: "Without the Qi within, the body stands hollow. And if hollow, how may life endure in it?"

**Paper Heron**: This takes real devotion. You must practice daily until your body is ready to harmonize with the flow of Qi.

**Paper Heron**: "To retain Qi is to attain the Way; one who has attained the Way may long endure," so the scripture says.

**Paper Heron**: But the path is long and perilous. Stray from it, and both body and spirit may be annihilated.

**Paper Heron**: At best, it is a process of decades; at worst, well, I've seen some wait hundreds of years.

**Hedgehog**: But, Grandmaster ...

**Paper Heron**: Yes? Speak your mind.

**Hedgehog**: Do you really mean it will take a few decades for us to master this method?

**Paper Heron**: To walk the path of longevity is no small feat. But the calmer your mind, the clearer your vision, and the quicker you will progress.

**Hedgehog**: But how can I devote myself to a method that takes decades to master when I only have a few years to live? And if what you say is true, wouldn't only the long-lived be able to achieve longevity?

**Paper Heron**: Ah!

She pauses, composing her thoughts for a long while, then walks over to the Gen trigram.

**Paper Heron**: Not entirely. The scripture says, "In the pursuit of worldly knowledge, one gains daily. In the pursuit of the Way, one loses daily. Less and less is done, until nothing is done. When nothing is done, nothing is left undone."

**Paper Heron**: Don't get so hung up on the path ahead. Nothing stays fixed forever. Live in the moment, and new opportunities will arise.

**Hedgehog**: So we'll just do nothing at all?

**Paper Heron**: Not exactly. It isn't nothing but rather "non-action." We let go of all deliberate effort, attending to your purposes, doing only that which is yours to do.

Hearing her words, the Yao look at each other. One of them cannot hold back their frustration and rushes up in front of her.

**Badger**: That's absurd!

**Badger**: If that's how it is, what are we to do? Sit around and wait for death to come? Our lives are much shorter than yours, you know!

**Yam**: Now, now, Brother Badger. The grandmaster didn't mean ...

Undeterred by the gentle redirection, the Yao continues his questions anyway.

**Badger**: "That which is yours to do." What's that supposed to mean? Is this "what's mine to do"?

**Hedgehog**: Grandmaster, none of us would be here if we had been content with the time we were given.

**Paper Heron**: Ah ...

Paper Heron is speechless. She sees now the crux of the issue; they have been led astray from the very beginning.

The doubting voices grow louder. The Yao become agitated. Paper Heron stands silent above them, lost. Mayfly struggles in her seat, not knowing who to agree with.

**Master Ren**: Alright, everyone.

A clear, loud call rings out like a stone dropped in water. The Yao immediately fall silent.

**Badger**: Master.

Master Rén walks into the ring and stands beside her teacher.

**Master Ren**: Each of us approaches the Way differently, for we are all guided by our own nature. The grandmaster speaks only from her own experience.

**Master Ren**: If her words help you, hold them. If they muddle you, do not be troubled. You may understand them in the time to come.

**Yam**: Yes, Master.

**Master Ren**: It's been a long day, and the grandmaster has traveled far. Please, leave her to rest.

Paper Heron looks at her former student and then at the calmed Yao. With a stiff nod, she resigns herself to a stone stool outside the ring.

**Mayfly**: Heron, are you alright?

She walks over and sits by Paper Heron, whose serene facade now seems ever so subtly broken.

**Paper Heron**: I'm fine. Should've chosen my words with more care, though.

**Mayfly**: Well ...

For a moment, the cicada chirps and bird calls sound unusually sharp.

Paper Heron looks down, hiding her face.

**Paper Heron**: I thought they'd be interested. Back in my time ...

The words are a faint whisper, so light she barely hears them.

**Mayfly**: What do you mean?

**Paper Heron**: Nothing. Just forget what I've said and follow your master's teachings.

**Paper Heron**: Perhaps she's found a better way.

**Master Ren**: The third step the grandmaster spoke of is what we call the "cultivation of the body." Through practice, your body will work with your Qi until they are one.

**Master Ren**: Mastering this may take decades, even hundreds of years, but here in the School of Mei, we needn't dwell on that step. Instead, we focus on the regulation of Qi, and concentration and visualization.

**Paper Heron**: ...

She looks over to Master Rén as she continues her lesson and resolves herself to what must be done.

**Paper Heron**: "We needn't dwell on that step"?

**Li Huifeng**: Why are you standing there like a statue? It's time to eat.

**Cheng Heguang**: I'm awaiting my sixty strokes.

Lì Huìfēng puts down the case file and looks at him with a complex expression.

**Li Huifeng**: *sigh* There won't be any coming. Now, go eat.

But he still does not move.

**Cheng Heguang**: If you've elected to spare me, then allow me a question, Commander.

**Cheng Heguang**: The man who came with you had a scroll in his hand. Where did it come from? There's a Bagua array on it, formed by a Mei tree and a jade sword.

**Li Huifeng**: Héguāng, if I spare you the punishment, you ought to at least do me the courtesy of sparing me the questions.

**Cheng Heguang**: Then I would rather take the punishment.

The evening wind blows through the hall, and the candlelight flickers in response.

**Li Huifeng**: Do you really have no inkling of who you offended tonight?

**Cheng Heguang**: I do not.

**Li Huifeng**: The Chén family, respected gentry with three Imperial Scholars in only a few decades. Lord Lù, a corps leader, his family have served in the military for generations. And the Lǐs—I needn't remind you who they are.

**Cheng Heguang**: I am but the son of bandits. I don't know any of these high lords.

**Li Huifeng**: Now you know.

Lì Huìfēng looks away and reads from the case file.

**Cheng Heguang**: The man with the scroll—is he of noble birth, too?

He does not receive an answer.

**Cheng Heguang**: Am I right to assume that you've kept me from investigating the School of Mei, not because you feared I might alarm them, but because you are aware of the school's prestigious background?

The words are pointed but do not break his commander's grim silence.

**Cheng Heguang**: You know they're responsible for the turmoil in the county, yet you permit these men to walk free, allowing the common Yao to take the fall—

**Li Huifeng**: Enough!

Lì Huìfēng rises with an expression as fiery as a lit rocket as he throws the files to the ground.

**Li Huifeng**: Are you so naive? Do you truly have no clue as to why you were spared today?

**Cheng Heguang**: Because of your connection to the man with the scroll.

**Li Huifeng**: Then you do have some inkling of what's going on!

**Li Huifeng**: You did well capturing those Yao, and I had planned to speak highly of you before Lord Lù. But after your actions today—storming into a civilian's home, attempting to arrest all present—how can I possibly recommend you!?

**Li Huifeng**: Have you forsaken your vow and decided to live in your father's disgrace forever?

**Cheng Heguang**: I would never!

He grits his teeth but does not give an inch.

**Cheng Heguang**: But Commander, this is more important than my name. This is for the safety of the townspeople!

**Li Huifeng**: Alright. Then tell me exactly what harm the School of Mei has done and what crime you accuse them of.

**Cheng Heguang**: As my prior report states, they are practicing sorcery and other forbidden arts.

**Li Huifeng**: They fabricated the descent of a deity at the parade, yes. But have you caught any of the offenders from that day?

**Cheng Heguang**: Not yet.

**Li Huifeng**: And has any member of the school actually committed a crime? Or have you found some scripture that proves their evil intention?

**Cheng Heguang**: ...

**Cheng Heguang**: I have not.

**Li Huifeng**: So you have nothing. You wish me to convince the magistrate to act against the School of Mei, risking the anger of officials and high lords based on nothing? Hm?

**Li Huifeng**: The school will claim that they were only teaching the methods to strengthen the body and enrich the mind, and that the Yao were foolish and greedy to think their practices could grant longevity.

**Li Huifeng**: We cannot act on hearsay and rumors, especially when it may anger the high lords!

**Cheng Heguang**: You're right. I lack the evidence to refute your words.

**Cheng Heguang**: But if it is the lords that worry you, I will investigate in secret. Three days is all I need. I will find the proof.

**Li Huifeng**: Enough.

Another cold blast of wind sweeps through the hall, rustling the papers on his desk.

Lì Huìfēng uses a paperweight to smooth the files and sits back into his chair.

**Li Huifeng**: Go now. Get some rest.

**Li Huifeng**: Your men are to be placed under the captain, Zhāng; he knows the county well. You will remain, but only as his backup.

**Cheng Heguang**: Why? I've done nothing wrong!

**Li Huifeng**: *sigh* Then you've not listened to a word I've said.

The water in the pot boils, the lid rattles, the steam whistles, and Lì Huìfēng pays it no attention.

Steam fills Chéng Héguāng's sight.

The pot at last boils over.

**Cheng Heguang**: Commander!

**Cheng Heguang**: Must the people's blood be spilled before we act?

**Li Huifeng**: Watch your tongue!

In the tea bowl on the desk, weak ripples form.

**Cheng Heguang**: ...

The young man stands solid, silent for a long time, rooted like a tree as the steam fades from him.

At last, he breaks the roots and turns.

**Cheng Heguang**: Perhaps I have not listened, Commander.

**Cheng Heguang**: Goodnight.

> 【Title card】Cheng's House, Ancient Zhu County

The cool moon shines like a lantern over a dark lake.

Chéng Héguāng puts down a book and rubs his tired neck.

**Cheng Heguang**: *sigh* It's getting late.

He lights a blackened torch with a candle, holding the light as he steps into the dark.

**Cheng Heguang**: Zhòngní said, "One of virtue follows the course of the Mean; one of cunning turns from it."

**Cheng Heguang**: "Following the Mean, the virtuous acts in due measure. Turning from the Mean, the cunning moves without restraint."

He stops at the door, deep in thought.

**Cheng Heguang**: Fortunately, it's still not too late.

A street cat cries out nearby.

**Cheng Heguang**: Hm? That's ...

**Night Watch**: Fire! Fire!

A man runs in panic. Behind him, plumes of smoke leap and billow into the sky.

**Night Watch**: There's a fire at Chief Constable Chéng's house!

### 3410114 A Sow's Ear {#episode-3410114}

> Subtitle: To think the old man believed he'd make a silk purse of it.


> 【Title card】Side Room, School of Mei

Inside the room, a few Yao gather around Mayfly, helping her trim the fresh herbs she picked from the mountains.

**Yam**: Now that you know the path, you can go up the hill at your leisure and gather the elixir ingredients yourself. A little walk in the forest will do you good.

**Mayfly**: Thank you. I know the elixir helps with the practice, but isn't it a little unsettling, harvesting these herbs like this?

**Yam**: What's the matter? They're only plants, too young to form any spirit yet. It's not as if you're cutting down one of your own.

**Paper Heron**: Mayfly! Oh, uh, I mean Sister Mayfly, I thought that I should come check on you. See how you're getting on.

**Mayfly**: Look at that. Someone finally discovered the door. Though not much of a knocker, are you?

**Yam**: Good day, Grandmaster.

Paper Heron nods to the Yao, then walks around Mayfly, looking left and right.

**Mayfly**: What? What is it? You're giving me the withers.

**Paper Heron**: You've followed Rén's teachings for a few days now, hm? How do you feel?

**Mayfly**: Heron, you've asked me this a few times already.

**Mayfly**: I'm well, just as I was yesterday and the day before that. My strength's improving. I feel light and full of energy, even after a long day in the mountains.

Paper Heron puts her hands behind her back and circles Mayfly two more times, nodding each time.

**Paper Heron**: That's good. That's good then. Are you certain everything's fine? Nothing feels strange at all?

**Mayfly**: Absolutely!

Mayfly pats her chest as if to prove her health.

**Mayfly**: Why do you keep asking? Is something troubling you?

**Paper Heron**: Nothing makes me happier than seeing you well. But may I ask have you felt anything out of place while practicing Rén's methods?

**Mayfly**: Out of place? I don't know. But I've moved on to the second stage, "concentration and visualization."

She sits in a meditation pose and makes a hand gesture to cast an incantation.

**Mayfly**: Master Rén said that to meditate, I must sit in silence, concentrating my mind on an object and visualizing the inner deities until I find their presence. With consistent practice, the path to longevity will reveal itself.

**Mayfly**: That Mei tree nearby really is an ideal object to focus on. It seems to have been there for over a thousand years. Maybe it really does have a connection to the spiritual world.

**Paper Heron**: Are those her words?

**Mayfly**: Her exact words! I meditate about that tree day and night. I even see it in my dreams sometimes.

**Mayfly**: And Master Rén has been most generous. She even helps the other students using the power of her sword. How did she explain it?

**Mayfly**: Something like using the sword to clear the blockage in their body, freeing the flow of Qi, so they can advance more quickly with their training.

**Mayfly**: The first time I saw it, I almost thought she was about to poke a few holes in me. But instead, she just swiped it above my head, just like you did at the parade.

**Mayfly**: I even asked Brother Yam to teach me something from the third stage. You should see how well I can do it already.

**Mayfly**: Posture one, "Breeze in the Lungs." Face north, feet spread as wide as the shoulders.

She chants the words and shows Paper Heron what she has learned.

**Mayfly**: Master Rén told us that we must cultivate our bodies to align with the movement of Qi. Only then can our mortal flesh be prepared for longevity.

**Mayfly**: She said the cultivation would take about two months.

**Paper Heron**: Two months? Those were her words?

**Mayfly**: That's right.

Hearing Mayfly's words, Paper Heron's face changes. A hint of sternness cuts across her brow.

**Butterfly**: *panting*

Butterfly bursts in, panting and waving his hands.

**Butterfly**: Wonderful news! Karma finally came for that heartless Chief Constable Chéng!

**Paper Heron**: Chéng?

Hearing this, the other Yao gather around.

**Hedgehog**: You mean that grumpy, self-righteous constable that's been hunting us night and day?

**Yam**: I heard that he's been interrogating Yao, plucking his captive's hairs one by one.

**Butterfly**: Yes, that's him. What a pig! No offense to pigs!

**Butterfly**: I guess brutality must run in his blood. His family used to be bandits until they worked their way into the military. Not that they lasted long as soldiers. His own father turned out to be a crook!

**Butterfly**: He cut ties with his father to keep his post. But I don't believe it. If he's willing to throw us all behind bars just to make himself look good, then he's just as bad as the rest of them!

**Yam**: I'll bet he's rotten to the core. But what do you mean by "karma came for him"? Ah, tell us what happened.

Butterfly seizes the moment with excitement as he proceeds to describe the fire at the chief constable's home.

**Mayfly**: Isn't that the man we met at the gate?

**Paper Heron**: I believe so.

Her response is quick and muted, intending not to interrupt the clamor of the Yao.

**Mayfly**: I just don't understand why he hates us so much. We haven't hurt anyone. We just want to spread the Method of Longevity.

**Hedgehog**: Hardly a surprise. Those with long lives seldom care for the short-lived.

The words bring a harsh chill to the air as the other Yao look at each other and then to Paper Heron.

**Yam**: Hedgehog! The grandmaster is still here.

**Paper Heron**: Please, speak your mind. It is every creature's right.

Her words do little to break the sudden chill until Butterfly steers things back on topic.

**Butterfly**: Oh! I nearly forgot that awful chief had nearly locked up our grandmaster!

**Butterfly**: Grandmaster, did you start the fire to avenge us?

**Paper Heron**: Haha. No, I didn't. Though if anyone questions you on the matter, you may give them my name.

**Butterfly**: Grandmaster ...

Hearing this, all the Yao look at Paper Heron with awe.

**Butterfly**: It is a great honor to study under an avenging hero like you.

**Butterfly**: Please accept our humblest gratitude.

**Yam**: Thank you. Thank you for your heroic deeds.

**Paper Heron**: Aha ...

Their undeserved praise lands somewhere between funny and vexing, yet she can't help but realize the situation is growing beyond her control.

**Yam**: The grandmaster has taken our interests to heart, and we must repay her with our greatest effort. We must achieve longevity and spread the school's name.

**All Yao**: Achieve longevity! Spread the school's name!

The room has become a hubbub of cheers and excitement. But Mayfly does not seem to be participating. She stares up blankly, spots dancing in her vision like fireflies at dusk.

**Mayfly**: Huh, I ... What's going on?

**Yam**: Mayfly? Are you alright?

In a moment, Mayfly feels the world spin beneath her feet.

**Paper Heron**: ...!

As she tumbles, she sees Paper Heron glide toward her. Then all goes dark.

> 【Title card】Yamen, Ancient Zhu County

The next day's sun rises as usual, but the Yamen's constables have a new topic to discuss.

**Constable I**: Did you hear? Those gentlemen we met yesterday have all fallen ill.

**Constable I**: It seems they've all been taken by a strange fever. Some fainted in an instant, while others went running and yelling on the streets in their undergarments. It was chaos.

**Constable I**: The chief was right. Whatever they were doing must have been dangerous.

**Constable II**: But I heard they hired a Daoist who cured them with nothing but water and a pinch of talisman ashes.

**Constable I**: Hmph. Well, that was easy. Shame the chief wasn't so lucky. To think a man could lose his home simply for doing his duty!

**Constable II**: Well, we don't know what caused the fire, do we?

**Constable I**: What else could it be? You were there. I think the chief found something important, and now they're desperate to get rid of him.

**Constable II**: I'm just glad I was on guard duty.

A shadow passes before the two men. They're struck silent with fear. But Chéng Héguāng does not even seem to notice them as he walks straight into the Yamen hall.

From his high seat, Lì Huìfēng looks at a plaque on the wall.

**Li Huifeng**: Héguāng, I understand it was your house that caught fire last night.

**Cheng Heguang**: It was.

**Li Huifeng**: It's a great relief to see you unharmed.

**Li Huifeng**: But I'm sorry for your loss. Take a few days. Find another place to stay and get some rest, will you?

**Cheng Heguang**: Much appreciated, Commander. That is precisely why I came.

Chéng Héguāng bows and then pours out his prepared words. It's clear immediately that he's had little rest.

**Cheng Heguang**: I was up late reviewing some case files. As it happened, the arsonists startled a cat as they approached. I was able to spy them from my window. Though I couldn't stop them in time.

**Cheng Heguang**: They were all Yao. I'm quite certain of it, as retaliation for the arrests I've made.

**Cheng Heguang**: Commander Lì, if I, a trained officer, couldn't protect my home from their schemes, what hope do the ordinary townspeople have?

**Cheng Heguang**: Please, permit me to bring them to justice and anyone else who shields them!

**Li Huifeng**: You—

**Cheng Heguang**: I know the Yamen is short-staffed. I won't ask for anyone's help until I have solid evidence.

**Cheng Heguang**: Now, I must take my leave. Good day, Commander!

He does not wait for Lì Huìfēng to say more and turns to leave.

High above them, the Yamen's bell is stirred by the wind, ringing out a long, clear note.

### 3410115 Into the Fire {#episode-3410115}

> Subtitle: But I don't have a choice.


After breakfast, several Yao gather around Mayfly's bed.

**Yam**: Mayfly, you were out for the whole day!

**Hedgehog**: Brother Yam told me you were unwell, so I brought some sweet cakes. I thought you might like something to eat after your fall.

**Mayfly**: Hmm. Thank you.

Still half-asleep, Mayfly responds in a weak voice.

**Paper Heron**: Mayfly, it's me again.

**Paper Heron**: I've brought herbs to replenish your Qi. Don't worry. I checked. All cut from plants. No Yao were harmed.

**Yam**: Greetings, Grandmaster!

The Yao greet her enthusiastically. She nods to each of them in turn, then sets a bundle of herbs on the table.

**Paper Heron**: Ah, no need for those formalities, please. Would you give Mayfly and me a moment in private?

**Yam**: Of course. We'll leave you two alone.

**Yam**: Don't you hear the grandmaster? Come on, let's go.

The Yao nudge each other out of the room. Before long, only Paper Heron and Mayfly remain.

**Mayfly**: Paper Heron?

She senses something unusual about the moment and turns her head to find Paper Heron wearing a dour expression.

**Paper Heron**: Mayfly, you must stop practicing Rén's method.

**Mayfly**: Why?

**Paper Heron**: Your Qi is too unstable. At times, it surges like a boar, and at others, it falters. Haven't you noticed?

**Mayfly**: I ...

**Paper Heron**: You know I'm right, don't you? Your fall before was a warning. Your Qi is in decline.

**Mayfly**: But I've felt so much more energetic lately. Even my mind feels clearer than before.

**Paper Heron**: Yes. You have learned a great deal about how to control your Qi. You'd be in great shape, if that were all you were practicing.

**Paper Heron**: For you to advance further, your Qi must align with the Way, and your body must be strong enough to carry it.

**Paper Heron**: But if you're too weak, your Qi can become too great a burden. It could consume you.

**Paper Heron**: In the White Horse School, we always ensured our physique was strong enough to handle each step along the path.

**Paper Heron**: But Rén is moving too fast, pushing you forward with the power of the Longevity Sword. It's possible you may still succeed in the end, but ...

**Paper Heron**: You're risking both body and spirit for a tiny possibility.

**Paper Heron**: You could end up with nothing. Your body destroyed, your spirit extinguished. You need to stop and allow your body to recover.

**Mayfly**: For how long? Days? Weeks? Months?

**Paper Heron**: Given your condition, I'd say two months before you resume any training.

**Mayfly**: Two months?

**Mayfly**: Do you realize how little time I have? Winter's coming. I can't wait that long.

**Paper Heron**: I know.

**Paper Heron**: But if you continue in this fashion, I fear you may not live to see the winter.

**Paper Heron**: I can't stand by and watch you destroy yourself. Not just you. All the Yao. This isn't the right path for any of you.

**Mayfly**: Heron ...

**Mayfly**: I know, to you, two months may seem like nothing. I suppose it may seem like years pass you by in the blink of an eye, don't they?

**Paper Heron**: ...

Paper Heron gazes at the girl propped halfway up in bed. Her lips tremble faintly before she finally speaks.

**Paper Heron**: It's not quite as fleeting as a blink of an eye.

**Mayfly**: What would you do over the course of a year?

**Paper Heron**: I—

**Mayfly**: Wander the roads on your mule, through cloud-covered mountains, across gentle streams, beneath fragrant blooming peach trees.

**Mayfly**: And when the year ends, you'd go to Huanzhou for the temple fair, feeling the warmth of the flames dancing against your face, savoring the floral sweetness of sticky rice cakes.

**Mayfly**: Next year you'll travel further still, to see snow-covered plains, brush the fur of a moose, taste wine so strong that it burns your throat.

**Mayfly**: You never worry about the days you spend on the road or whether you have enough time to experience all the world has to offer.

The words hang bitterly on her lips, soon accompanied by wet tears flowing down her face.

**Mayfly**: But I won't live a full cycle of seasons.

One drop, two drops, three drops. The bedding covering her grows damp with a steady flow of tears.

Paper Heron can do nothing to stem their flow. So, she simply waits, watching her friend in tender silence.

**Mayfly**: To you, a day, a month, a year, it means nothing.

**Mayfly**: But for Yao like me, a year is a lifetime—our only lifetime.

**Mayfly**: I want to live, even just a little longer, to see more, feel more. I can't allow myself to waste even a moment.

**Mayfly**: In a thousand years, my name could still be carved on that stone. But I won't live to know if it's there next spring. So, why must you stop me?

**Paper Heron**: ...

There are barbs on the question, too sharp to swallow, too true to ignore. She chews on it a long while, hoping to reach an answer.

**Paper Heron**: I didn't intend to hurt your feelings when I carved that stone.

**Paper Heron**: Is it your wish then? To live as long as the stones?

**Mayfly**: What? What do you mean?

Paper Heron smiles, but a trace of sorrow lingers at the corners of her mouth.

**Paper Heron**: Besides Inner Alchemy and Rén's method, there is a third way to escape the flow of time, one that has been kept a secret.

**Paper Heron**: It doesn't take hundreds of years of training, nor does it endanger your Qi. All it costs is your school, a sword, and a hundred years sealed in a tree.

**Paper Heron**: When the seal breaks, all you once knew will be gone—friends and enemies alike. You will no longer laugh nor hate, and your senses will dull.

**Paper Heron**: Sweet or sour, salt or spice, it will all taste the same.

**Paper Heron**: People will cheer at the blazing fire flowers, yet to you, the flames will be as mild as a passing breeze, their excitement like a language you no longer understand.

**Paper Heron**: Your memories will stay. You'll always recall how the morning mist felt on your face, the crispness of spring water as it flowed through your fingers, but you will never feel them again.

**Paper Heron**: You will become like a stone. Is that what you want?

**Mayfly**: Is that how the world feels to you?

**Paper Heron**: ...

She doesn't reply.

Mayfly lowers her head, her fingers twisting together as if trying to hold the weight of her tangled thoughts.

After a moment's consideration, she takes something from her pocket.

It's the amulet that was trampled by her and repaired by Paper Heron.

**Mayfly**: But Heron, you've already shown me a way.

**Mayfly**: This amulet—I spent every coin I had on it, just for a chance to get through the city gate.

**Mayfly**: It didn't work like I'd hoped, and I felt so foolish for believing in it. But you repaired it, even improved it, so that I could make it through.

**Mayfly**: I may be just a wind-tossed reed, but that doesn't mean I'm unworthy of the wonders of this world. Isn't that what you wanted to tell me?

**Mayfly**: I'm willing to take the chance to lose everything or gain the world.

**Mayfly**: You once said that fate presents an opportunity to every one of us.

**Mayfly**: You've had yours, and I need to take mine.

**Paper Heron**: You mean that you want to follow Rén's method no matter the danger?

**Mayfly**: Yes.

**Mayfly**: *cough* She-She has shown us a way to live beyond our years.

**Mayfly**: Even if it's dangerous, I want to take the chance to truly live.

**Paper Heron**: ...

**Paper Heron**: I understand.

She knows it won't be useful to argue her point any longer. She rises to her feet and taps the herbs on the table.

**Paper Heron**: Just remember to drink my herbal brew, eh?

The door stands ajar. Other Yao peer inside with curiosity. Paper Heron walks past them without a word.

In the dazzling morning light, she walks straight toward the courtyard.

### 3410116 To Heaven! {#episode-3410116}

> Subtitle: Not just longevity, but immortality.


##### `【3.4】不老春16.1` (script `203422`)

Morning light renders the Mei petals nearly translucent under the sun. Beneath the Mei tree, young Yao practice in formation.

**Paper Heron**: Where is your master?

**School of Mei Believer I**: Grandmaster Heron, I believe she left to attend to some personal matters.

**Paper Heron**: Erm, I think it best you no longer call me that. Your master has taken a path away from my teachings. I am now nothing more than an ordinary Daoist to you.

**School of Mei Believer I**: Oh, I see.

They exchange worried glances, but seeing the pain beneath her smile, they choose not to trouble her.

**Paper Heron**: When she returns, please tell her that I want to have a word with her here. Is there a place we could speak?

**School of Mei Believer I**: Certainly, Grand, uh, I mean, Master Heron.

White clouds drift past the sun, casting shadows eastward.

After roughly half a day, Master Rén returns to the school. Before the Mei tree, Paper Heron stands alone.

**Master Ren**: You wish to speak with me?

**Paper Heron**: I do. The day's been quiet, and I've found myself reminiscing on the old days. Would you join me for a chat beneath the Mei tree?

She smiles as she gestures toward the tree in the courtyard.

**Master Ren**: This tree?

Master Rén glances at the red Mei tree. It's scrawny for its years. Staring up at it, she can't help but laugh coldly.

**Master Ren**: Why? There isn't much to it. It could take a thousand years before it rivals the largest Mei tree in town.

**Paper Heron**: Let's just talk about the old days, eh?

**Paper Heron**: When the White Horse School attempted to subdue the Beast Lǎnzhū, they were taken by surprise by rival schools. We lost all our most capable masters in the battle.

**Master Ren**: A hundred years later, a Painted-Skin Yao faced her celestial tribulation under the same tree. Lightning struck both her and the tree, and the seal was broken.

**Master Ren**: The lightning nearly destroyed the Yao. The White Horse student, freed from the seal and surprised by such a turn of fate, saved the dying Yao and taught her the Daoist arts. We both know the story.

**Paper Heron**: Yes, you remember every detail of it.

**Master Ren**: I could never forget.

**Paper Heron**: I gave you the remaining sword and taught you the way of Inner Alchemy, but I never asked you to take the name of a White Horse student. I knew the school was lost to history.

**Master Ren**: The school is gone, yes, but their duty to control the Xiǎndào Beast was unfinished.

**Master Ren**: What's the purpose of this, Heron?

She shakes her head, gazing out into the distance toward another giant Mei tree far beyond their sight—a sister of the school's own centerpiece.

**Paper Heron**: What is your purpose, Rén?

**Paper Heron**: You told your students to channel their Qi into the Mei tree. Why?

Her old student looks at her and simply laughs.

**Master Ren**: So you've found out about that.

**Paper Heron**: I'm not easily fooled.

Master Rén lets the words roll over her as she settles herself at the stone table beneath the tree's shadow.

**Master Ren**: I know you disagree with my methods, but whether you agree or not, this is what is best for the students.

**Master Ren**: They're not like you. None of them have the talent or lifespan to properly cultivate longevity.

**Master Ren**: Had you been in my place, you likely wouldn't have taken them on at all. But I want to give them a chance.

**Master Ren**: After all, what would a talented master like you know of the life of a lowly Yao, of our struggles and desires?

**Paper Heron**: I do not mean to question your teachings, Rén. I only need to know why you've focused their Qi there, of all places.

**Master Ren**: My, my, when did you become so impatient, Heron?

*ching*

Master Rén casts a familiar incantation, and the white sword reappears in the air.

**Master Ren**: You trusted me with the sword, and I have endeavored to honor that trust by sharing it. I was once a short-lived Yao myself. It is only natural that I wish to help my kind.

**Master Ren**: Combining Inner Alchemy with the power of the Longevity Sword, I developed a method for our kind to overcome their disadvantages.

**Master Ren**: The sword can hold and release Qi. It gives, and it takes. Through it, I work to bring the Yao the lives they deserve.

**Master Ren**: Should they succeed, there will be one more Daoist master to carry the Method forward.

**Master Ren**: And if they fail, their remaining Qi is gathered within the Mei tree to aid us in subduing the beast when it next awakens. Either way, the outcome is favorable.

**Master Ren**: And either way, their deaths will not be in vain.

**Paper Heron**: You lay it out so plainly. Do your students know?

**Paper Heron**: Do they know their master sees them as mere fuel for her designs?

**Master Ren**: Does any price we pay matter if it means subduing the beast?

She laughs again, but there's no joy in it. Paper Heron turns her head away.

**Master Ren**: "No matter the cost," I said. I gave you my word. This is but a small portion of the sacrifices I am prepared to make.

- **"This city is ours."** (`element 3510106`)
  - Description: Everyone knows exactly what to avoid.
  - Unlock: `EpisodeFinish=3510103`

  > 【Title card】The City and the "City"

  - After the "Storm," the Vigiles Bureau returns to every "important city" following the same pattern—an unremarkable office at first, then a few Vigils, and before long, people simply grow accustomed to its presence as though it has always belonged there.  
  
According to official records, the Vigiles Bureau exists to investigate complex cases involving arcanum. It operates independently of the government, each fulfilling its own mandate without interfering with the other's affairs, though the two maintain steady communication.  
  
At the same time, the criminal underworld enters what the press calls the age of "modern crime." The most dangerous example of which is known as "El Automóvil Gris" or the Grey Car Gang, driving in their eponymous automobiles with matching grey attire. Their increasingly organized robberies and violence have given them a steady spot in the crime columns. Their methods have been dissected and debated at length, yet no amount of analysis softens the reality of what they are. People have begun to realize that violence and plunder are becoming more organized and more efficient. Crime is no longer a matter for the police alone—it has become a reality the whole of society can no longer afford to ignore.  
  
Of course, the Grey Car Gang alone is not enough to shake the order of an entire city. The local police know the limits of their authority, and the Vigiles Bureau understands how to avoid raising questions outside its jurisdiction. The underworld and the authorities share the same map—they simply disagree on how to read it.  
  
This seemingly harmonious coexistence does not eliminate conflict, only confines it. Police, Vigils, and grey cars pass through the same streets, fully aware of one another. They all understand the same unspoken truth—when the sun rises, the streets return to normal. Everything dissolves into the daylight, folding back into the city's shadow.

- **Beneath the Dust** (`element 3510107`)
  - Description: The art and culture we're crying out for.
  - Unlock: `EpisodeFinish=3510103`

  > 【Title card】The Muralism Movement, Part I

  - In early twentieth-century Mexico, no art form is more woven into everyday life than the art of the mural. Too large for any private collection, they occupy stairwells, courtyards, and corridors. It is for this reason that the muralism movement sparks continuous debate—about art itself, about who gets to decide how art is presented, and about how long these works can remain in public spaces.  
  
There was a time when the government dictated the direction of aesthetics. Only when the old order collapses do suppressed traditions find new life. Public buildings become canvases. Images naturally take on the role of narrative and expression. Murals spread across corridors and courtyards, functioning less like paintings meant to be admired and more like street signs or door plaques. Across different works, the same gestures appear again and again—heads raised, hands at labor, bodies in motion. Learning to read these images becomes part of life in the city and beyond. Through this art, Mexicans begin to build an entirely new sense of identity.  
  
In technique, most of these works take the form of frescos. The painter works against the drying plaster. Pigments sink into the wall and allow almost no revision once set. Over time, colors gradually fade and outlines disappear beneath dust. Countless people pass beneath them, look up briefly, and walk on. Yet the walls remain, still bearing the traces.  
  
Perhaps the mural's true significance lies not in its form or technique, but in the emotion and memory it carries.

#### Trail

- **Ancient Calendar** (`element 3510113`)
  - Description: Will we see the sixth sun?
  - Unlock: `EpisodeFinish=3510108`

  > 【Title card】The Story of the Sun Stone

  - The Aztec Sun Stone is often called the "Aztec Calendar." But it's really more of a cosmic map carved in basalt—or, as the Aztecs understood it, a guide to how the world works.  
  
The stone was unearthed in Mexico City in the 18th century. It measures over 3.5 meters across and weighs more than 20 tons. The center of the Sun Stone is Tōnatiuh, the god of the sun. His gaze is stern, his outstretched tongue carved to resemble a Tecpatl. The message is clear: offer the sun your most precious gift—your blood—or receive nothing in return.  
  
The concentric rings around Tōnatiuh record the four "suns" that came before—one transformed into a jaguar and devoured the people, one engulfed the world in a hurricane, one rained fire from the heavens, and the last drowned the world in a massive flood. Each sun's reign ended in an apocalypse, and none of their subjects survived.  
  
Moving outward, you'll find religious symbols, patterns marking the cycle of day and night, and colors representing celestial bodies ... They unfold layer by layer, like a cosmic machine disassembled and laid bare—precise, ancient, orderly. Together, they capture the Aztec understanding of the world: the universe resets, all things are reborn, and humanity is nothing more than a speck of dust within it.

#### Trail

- **The Necessary Step** (`element 3510118`)
  - Description: We gather, we part—all because of a single word.
  - Unlock: `EpisodeFinish=3510117`

  > 【Title card】Murals and Turning Points

  - This is a land where traditions are told through murals. After the revolution, the young government turned to its artists. This newborn Mexico had so many stories to tell, so many to shape—and paintings adorning the walls of its buildings became the perfect medium. In the 1920s, the muralist movement swept through the country.  
  
Look, this was an art form both ancient and brand new. It no longer lived in auction houses, galleries, or the private collections of the wealthy. Instead, it unfolded across vast walls open to the public. On those walls, artists spoke of justice, of freedom, of this nation's history and memory. Imagine it! A new country, a new canvas, and so many stories to tell! From the very beginning, these murals were inseparable from politics. The brush was the artist's voice. They spoke for their ideals, for beauty, for all the suffering people of the world ...  
  
But voices are difficult to harmonize. And they can turn harsh.  
  
As the 20th century entered its third decade, cracks began to appear—between artist and artist, between artist and state. Should the murals depict suffering or glory? Whose praises should they sing? Which path forward? Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros—three names that once symbolized hope, our "Los Tres Grandes"—held different visions for the future of both their art and their country.  
  
The rifts only deepened. In the small "Midnight Kitchen," young painters listened to this "fight of the century."

### 3510119 Metaphor {#episode-3510119}

The man shows no fear as he turns toward the assassin.

The two of them speak with the same casual ease.

**Lorentz Butterfly**: How could he have planned and executed all this, alone, in such a state?

**Lorentz Butterfly**: Finding eight suitable targets among hundreds of thousands in Mexico City, coaxing them to accept paintings they probably had no interest in.

**Lorentz Butterfly**: Each step required meticulous observation and careful planning.

She laughs softly but without a trace of warmth.

**Lorentz Butterfly**: You lured her to this mural, intending to offer her as the final sacrifice to fulfill your ultimate wish.

His response is muted. There's almost a hint of surprise, but it rests beneath his calm composure.

**Añil**: That's all you want to ask? I see.

**Añil**: Your deductions are perfect, of course, Ms. Butterfly. I am merely an amateur by comparison.

**Lorentz Butterfly**: I'll be sure to keep your insights in mind.

A pistol.

A Luger P08. Practical for self-defense. A precise, purely scientific creation.

**Marcus**: It was just like the one you brought: a beautifully arranged bouquet of white chrysanthemums.

**Semmelweis**: And Enigma? Where's he gone off to? Weren't they each other's only family?

**Semmelweis**: But now, at that very sister's funeral, our Mr. Adler is nowhere to be found.

**Marcus**: Then he left all in a hurry.

**Marcus**: Later, I received word from Laplace that he'd barred the door to his office.

**Semmelweis**: Hah. So he's chosen escapism, then.

The conversation ends there.

He, the two of them, and all the rest gathered here are little more than acquaintances to one another.

Familiar only in their mourning.

**Marcus**: ...

At last, Marcus speaks again.

**Marcus**: There was a mailing list among Madam Hofmann's possessions.

**Marcus**: On the train to Vienna, she asked me a question, hoping I could "read" its answer.

**Hofmann**: "What is the best way for someone to defend themselves if they cannot use arcane skills?"

**Marcus**: I read the answer she expected. She asked because she was preparing a gift.

The words fly out of her like fired bullets.

What a rare thing, the chance to ease unbearable grief simply by sharing it.

**Marcus**: Mr. Enigma packed the list, her documents, her ID badge, and her diary into a box. Madam Hofmann's entire life ... reduced to a tiny box.

**Marcus**: Then he stopped. And he asked me—

**Enigma**: Where do you think Greta has gone?

The ink on the paper in her hand starts to run again.

**Marcus**: "Where has she gone? Heaven? Hell? Has this 'Storm' washed them away too?"

**Marcus**: "Those who aren't lost to the 'Storm'—where do they go?"

**Marcus**: Will I see her again someday? Will all of us, any of us, see her again?

**Marcus**: If only I'd known earlier that the gift she was preparing was a birthday present for him, then instead of taking care of me and celebrating my first day as a Foundation Investigator, she could have ...

**Marcus**: If only my arcane skill were more useful! If only I'd read what would happen on that stage!

**Marcus**: If only the future were written out as words on a page!

Semmelweis says nothing. She only raises her hand gently.

But before that touch can reach her, Marcus draws a deep breath and forces her "what ifs" back down.

There is nowhere to turn for answers. No point in blaming herself. What's done is done.

**Marcus**: ...

**Marcus**: I told him I hoped Madam Hofmann had gone somewhere with no "Storm" and started a new life, even if that means we'll never see her again.

**Marcus**: In the end, he said he needed to think about my answer. He hasn't left his room since.

**Marcus**: I can understand that. I don't want to be here either. But I have to, because I want people to know that they don't need to worry about me anymore.

**Marcus**: Escapism is a natural reaction to grief. Just because you don't want to face it doesn't mean you're heartless, don't you think?

She waits almost stubbornly for an answer.

Semmelweis glances toward the distant grave and smiles softly.

**Semmelweis**: Look at you saying all that without stammering. You see? There's no need to worry.

**Marcus**: ...?

**Marcus**: S-Sorry. I-I shouldn't have suddenly ...

**Semmelweis**: No, you're right. Everyone handles grief differently.

**Marcus**: *deep breath*

**Marcus**: Madam Hofmann was an exemplary Foundation Investigator, a dependable teammate, and my dearest mentor.

**Marcus**: She never cowered in the face of sacrifice. She followed ...

A hand settles on her back. Semmelweis finishes the sentence for her.

**Semmelweis**: She followed her own path until the end ...

**Marcus**: ... pursuing the truth with a resolute heart.

**Marcus**: And, ultimately, it was her fearlessness and perseverance that brought us the knot that allows us to cross the "Storm."

That's why I have to cherish every chance to keep the story going.

**Marcus**: She inspired many, none more than myself. She gave me the courage to leave the Flannan Isles, allowing me to witness and read so many new things. So standing here, I vow ...

**Marcus**: To continue to seek what she sought, what we all seek! A world after 1999!

Because I want to see the world you believed in.

**Marcus**: I will persevere as she did. I will keep reading, keep writing, record every experience, every feeling!

**Marcus**: I ...

**Marcus**: ... will never forget what you've done for us. For me.

  - To prevent Laplace employees from falling victim to pranks from colleagues and to avoid research delays from being unable to break codes, we are distributing this Beginner's Guide to Ciphers: Vigenère Edition.  
The Vigenère cipher can be seen as an upgrade to the Caesar cipher, turning the simple shift of a single alphabet into shifts across multiple alphabets to increase complexity. For more on the Caesar cipher, see the Caesar Cipher Edition.  
The main difference between the Vigenère and Caesar ciphers is that in the Vigenère cipher, the relationship between the ciphertext and plaintext letters isn't one-to-one, making the key harder to figure out. However, since it still follows patterns, you can still find repeating ciphertext segments. By using high-frequency words in common language, you can guess the plaintext for specific segments of ciphertext, deduce the key length from the spacing between repeats, and analyze the key.  
However, if you don't have much text, this can be difficult. In these situations, you should use other methods to guess the key. The personality, past, and writing habits of the person who made the code are important clues. Here is a list of people at Laplace who are very likely to play pranks with ciphers:  
  
Adler, Ulrich, X, Richard, Dawkins, Victor ...  
  
If you encounter a prank, consider these suspects first. If you can't crack the code, confront the suspects directly and ask them to stop the prank. If a suspect denies involvement, try to force them to decode it for you. It doesn't matter whether they're really the culprit or not.

**Enigma**: I'm afraid that's this toybox's version of the moon.

Enigma distances himself from the communicator as another wave of commotion erupts on the other end. A moment later, Ulrich's calm voice comes through.

**Enigma**: ...

**Enigma**: Ms. Marcus. Would you like to come with me?

Following the piece's direction, Enigma squints into the distance. The white tower's spire rises above a sea of treetops.

**Enigma**: Hah. How wonderfully eye-catching. What is this, Tantalus's punishment?

He knows this researcher. The toybox is pulling from his buried memories.

**Enigma**: It's me. A tiny, insignificant cryptographer.

**Enigma**: It's a pity we've never worked together.

The communicator rings again. Whether it's at the worst moment or the best one, he can't decide.

**Hissabeth**: Adler, how bad is it?

**Enigma**: Oh, fine. Just a piece who's gone mad.

**Enigma**: ...

The fortress crumbles. The metal dissolves like foam. Ludwig twitches on the ground.

**Ludwig**: You're not going to heed my warning, are you? You're still going to remove the core—to satisfy your curiosity.

  > 【Title card】Sequel · UTTU Scouting Trip

  - Crossing most of that vast building—the long corridors, the broad staircases, the open ground beneath its fallen dome—left me nearly spent. You can probably guess how I felt. I checked my notebook of hurried sketches one last time and told myself: "Just a little further—that tavern drink the locals talked about is waiting for you."  
Unsurprisingly, the "neighbors" were at the tavern too. The old woman behind the bar mixed me a quick drink. Beside me sat a man in an old postal uniform, blank-faced, his shoulders worn pale. A ragged, half-transparent canvas mailbag rested on his lap. It seemed I had a "ghost" for company.  
"You're welcome to move seats if he makes you uneasy. Old Michał never listens to anyone anyway," the old woman offered gently.  
I thanked her but stayed put. It was, after all, a good chance to rest while observing a "ghost." The old postman's shade sat in silence, staring at the grain of the bar counter, as if an after-work vodka should have been waiting there. Not far off, an old woman wrapped in a heavy shawl stood by a table, taking out the same photo—a photo-shaped shade—again and again, turning it over in her hands. I guessed she must have lived alone in some apartment block, in a room that always smelled of coal stove and old cloth.  
By the time I finished my drink and looked back, a man in work clothes was standing at the center of the empty tavern—I couldn't say when he'd arrived—as if he'd been waiting there for a hundred years, a thousand years. Half his face was burned, and I caught the faint scent of ash coming off him.  
Something about his face must have drawn me in, because I found myself standing, trying to speak with him.  
"Sir, if I may ask, what are you doing here?"  
"Waiting." His answer came out hoarse.  
"Waiting for whom?"  
"A woman with eyes as blue as Lake Baikal."  
"You're hurt, sir."  
"No ... this isn't a wound."  
"It's Her ... it's proof that God has forsaken us."  
He raised a hand to the burn scarring his cheek.  
"We were promised gold. That year, winter went on forever. I waved her goodbye and headed into the frozen wild.  
The workers labored on, day and night.  
Until the black oil erupted from the wells, flames rising and fading in the falling snow."  
His pupils trembled faintly, a silent fire burning somewhere in him.  
"Our sky broke open—but no dawn ever came."  
I think I knew where he'd come from. Everyone in this country knew where he and his scars came from.

"There it is. I thought I'd lost it for good."  
"I opened it by accident and saw the photo inside. You were beautiful back then. Eyes like lake water."  
"Thank you, Stasia."  
The click of metal opening. A gasp.  
"While we were surveying the building, we came across a man with burn scars on his face ... He told us he was waiting for a woman with eyes as blue as Lake Baikal."  
"Ah. So you've already met Tomasz."  
Another rustle of cloth. Knuckles clenching. A soft sigh.  
"He's always wandering this building—the stairs, the landings, my tavern. He's still wearing that old wool coat he had on the day I saw him off at the station.  
Even though he's long dead. What wanders here is just his ghost, his echo, whatever you want to call it—repeating the same few lines over and over even when I'm standing right in front of him."  
"I'm so ..."  
"No need to apologize, Stasia. You found my pendant for me—if anything, I owe you a few more drinks.

When they brought me the scraps of his clothes, I thought that was the end of everything. When I was exiled, I thought that was the end too ... And when the anomaly hit, I really thought it was over this time. But here I am. Even Tomasz is still here.  
"So ... life still goes on."

  - Sat Sunny  
We got a rare good day today! The sky's still gray, but I could actually see the sun. I woke up early, since Róża and I had agreed to meet at the flowerbed. I'd packed sliced black bread and pickles into my bag the night before. I couldn't wait, and after breakfast I ran straight there. Róża was already waiting for me, but Emil and Andrzej were late. We waited ten minutes for them, and Róża talked with me the whole time.  
We took the tram to the newly built steel factory. Emil and Andrzej wanted to see the chimney, and I wanted to sketch. It really was a huge chimney, like some beast breathing coal-fire smoke from its great mouth. Róża said that after all these years, Nowa Miedź finally having a factory this size is a good thing. I drew the chimney, the canal, and a few wildflowers. My river sketchbook keeps getting thicker. Andrzej said he thinks I'll become a river expert. But it's not the canal itself I want to draw, though it matters too, of course. Why do we build our houses by the river? Why do we build our factories by the river? Why does the canal bring more people here? Why does the river turn black? Could we live somewhere better? Róża's explained it all to me before, but I want to find the answers myself. Maybe once I've figured it all out, I can help Mum, Dad, and my friends live better lives.

  > 【Title card】The Story of a Brick

  - When I was still a student, I spent a year traveling, visiting buildings. I wandered the abandoned amphitheaters of Rome, its aqueducts and temples, sketching in the Mediterranean wind the way Brunelleschi and Donatello did in the 15th century. I was trying to find the essence, the true form of architecture, in those collapsed, unadorned ruins.  
Until at last I arrived in India. At the Indian Institute of Management, I met an old man with scars on his face. He told me a story about a brick and an arch.  
The architect asks the brick, "Brick, what do you want to be?"  
The brick says, "I want to be an arch."  
The architect says, "I want an arch too, but arches are too expensive. What if we use a concrete lintel instead?"  
Still, the brick tells you only this: "I want to be an arch."  
At the end of the story, the old man said, "It's important to respect the material you've chosen. If you're going to use this brick, the best way is to respect it, to let it become what it is, not just to make do with it."

  - Dear Olga,  
My warmest greetings to you, old friend!  
You might be surprised to get this letter. Marek and I wrote it together because we thought you'd want to know how we're doing. And we wanted to talk to you too—to our dear old neighbor, someone who still remembers that we come from Nowa Miedź.  
We're doing well in Gdańsk. The sky isn't gray here. We've rented a house near the north port and started a small business. Please, don't worry about us.  
It's hard to put into words how I survived those first years. At least three times a week, I'd wake up crying because I'd dreamed of that day, the last time I saw Lucjan. Even now, I still feel sick when I see one of those cattle cars. It was cars just like that one that swallowed my child. They split families up between different groups, and by the time I finally got off that train alive, I'd lost my son forever.  
Forgive me for writing about such painful things. But Lucjan loved you so much. I think about it often—if we could go back to Nowa Miedź, how he'd run straight into your arms, how he'd introduce you to his little sister. He never got to meet her. Maybe he's watching her from somewhere above.  
Which reminds me, I should introduce you to the newest member of our family—Maja. She was born two winters ago. I've included a photo of her with this letter. I wanted you to see her for yourself. She has my nose, Marek's eyes, and ears just like Lucjan's, the same shape that came down from my grandmother. I think Lucjan would be happy for us. He always wanted a little sister.  
We asked around for a long time, and finally a fellow countryman told us your address hadn't changed at all—still the one I remembered. I can't really describe how that felt to hear. You're a brave woman, Olga, and that's such a rare thing these days. We've all weathered the storm. No one escapes its ravages. I wish you health and good fortune, and that you and your family are well. Marek and I think of you often, and we hope that someday we'll see each other again.  
Always thinking of you,  
Katarzyna

  - They left a small gap around the doors and windows. This building has plenty of windows. If it could hold voices in, then departing souls should be able to pass through those same gaps and reach heaven, or so the elders said. The young architect nodded and covered the mirror, as her hometown's traditions demanded—so the living wouldn't glimpse their reflection and trap the dead among them.  
Someone should have done this for that boy years ago. He was left behind in the train car, among the exiled, in the very building he'd once lived in. This was a funeral long overdue.  
Jasio put on his best suit, the only foreign wool one he owned. Everyone who'd known the boy dressed in their finest. There was no coffin at this funeral, but people still gathered at the little bar and kept vigil for the boy all through the night. Candlelight rose soft and warm, lighting up the seat where he used to sit.  
"You're singing," said the girl with the hand puppet. "What should I sing?"  
They taught her how to sing a dirge. A wake needed no instruments, only song after song.  
At dawn, the people set out from the bar with white candles in hand, heading for the dome. The boy had wanted to see that dome finished.  
"Say something, Stasia. He'd want to hear it from you," the old woman said softly.  
The architect stepped forward and cleared her throat. The words caught there like fine sand—an itch she couldn't clear.  
"I won't forget Lucjan." She began with those words, as sunlight spilled gently through the broken dome, and it made her think of the light that boy had become. "He ... he's with us."

- **Before the Rain** (`element 3810113`)

  > 【Title card】"Living Electricity System"

  - "If blood turns to electric current, does the soul still stay in the body?"  
  
The blood vessels change first. They stop their soft pulsing and begin to grow straight, silent, climbing upward along the wrists—red, yellow, blue, green, black, and white gelcoat sheathing thin threads of metal, pushing slowly through skin, through flesh.  
  
The bakery clerk is the first to notice something wrong. She stops touching hot water. When the morning steam rises, her arms give off a faint glow, and in the places where blood should flow, something else now coils and branches quietly, like a tangle of wiring rewoven into place.  
  
More and more people fill the hospitals. X-rays line the light boxes. Inside the pale bodies there are no organs, only crisscrossing wires, like the vast, silent power grid beneath a city. The doctors say the humming in the chest, the numbness in the neck, and the teeth that flicker with light now and then—all of it is nothing but insomnia.  
  
Then even the chapel starts fizzing and crackling with prayer. The silver ornament on the host's chest is leaking current, throwing off tiny blue sparks. Someone weeps on their knees. Someone catches the smell of scorched metal in the air. An old woman looks up and quietly asks the question that has long lingered within her heart:  
  
"If blood turns to electric current, does the soul still stay in the body?"  
  
The host doesn't answer. A patch of bronze has surfaced on his palm too.

I. Background  
The Temporal Anomaly is a highly dangerous arcane spatiotemporal hazard. Any individual exposed within its area of effect will vanish instantly, without a trace.  
A building in the Nowa Miedź region holds extremely high strategic value. It has been confirmed that this building is capable of stably resisting the regressive effects of the Temporal Anomaly. Individuals within its enclosed structure are immune to the Temporal Anomaly's effects.  
  
II. Establishment of the Office  
On November 8, 1996, the St. Pavlov Foundation Nowa Miedź Office was formally completed. Its primary responsibilities include monitoring abnormal environmental energy, coordinating resident evacuations, and handling regional anomalous incidents.  
Across multiple disaster events, this facility has operated stably, with no reversion breach incidents recorded.
